no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

response:
{"headline": "SOLID-TIMI 52 failed to demonstrate that darapladib reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in post-ACS patients, consistent with a non-causal target (PLA2G7 genetic score 0.0).",
 "summary": "The SOLID-TIMI 52 trial randomized 13,026 patients after acute coronary syndrome to darapladib or placebo, targeting a 15.5% relative risk reduction in the composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke with 90% power and 1,500 planned events over 3 years. The trial did not meet its primary endpoint. Observed results from the related STABILITY programme (15,828 stable CHD patients, 3.7-year median follow-up, 1,588 events) showed a hazard ratio of 0.94 (95% CI 0.85–1.03), which includes the null. The calculator, incorporating zero human genetic support for PLA2G7 (association score 0.0), predicted an expected HR of 1.0 and a 2.5% probability of success, matching the observed failure. Phase 2 data confirmed robust target engagement (Lp-PLA2 activity inhibition of 80–81%), but genetics indicate the target itself is not causal for coronary artery disease. No major safety concerns were reported.",
 "key_evidence": [
  "Planned enrollment: 13,026 participants (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01000727 SOLID-TIMI 52)",
  "Primary endpoint: composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome.)",
  "Planned events: 1,500 primary end point events; power: 90%; assumed RRR: 15.5%; planned median follow-up: 3 years (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome.)",
  "Observed hazard ratio: 0.94 (95% CI 0.85–1.03) from 1,588 events (769 treatment, 819 control) in 15,828 patients over 3.7-year median follow-up (Darapladib for preventing ischemic events in stable coronary heart disease.)",
  "Trial readout: darapladib did not achieve the primary endpoint of a reduction of major coronary events versus placebo (GSK announces phase III study with darapladib did not meet primary endpoint in patients following an acute coronary syndrome (13 May 2014))",
  "Phase 2 biomarker engagement: Lp-PLA2 activity inhibited by 80–81% (Effect of darapladib treatment on endarterectomy carotid plaque lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 activity: a randomized, controlled trial.)",
  "Genetic evidence: PLA2G7 association score 0.0 (opentargets:PLA2G7)",
  "Calculator prediction: expected HR 1.0, causal RRR 0.0, probability of success 2.5% (calculator)",
  "Safety: no major safety concerns; no significant between-group differences in all-cause mortality (GSK announces phase III study with darapladib did not meet primary endpoint in patients following an acute coronary syndrome (13 May 2014); Darapladib for preventing ischemic events in stable coronary heart disease.)"
 ],
 "what_would_change_this": "Human genetic evidence linking PLA2G7 variants that alter Lp-PLA2 activity to coronary artery disease risk would be required to support target causality and justify further development.",
 "readthrough_note": "The parallel STABILITY trial in stable coronary heart disease showed an identical null result (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.85–1.03), reinforcing that Lp-PLA2 inhibition does not translate into clinical benefit across coronary disease populations."}
